articles.title: No trains between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria this week as replacement buses run
articles.excerpt: Passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are being advised to allow extra time this week, with trains replaced by buses from Monday 10 to Friday 14 August.
articles.content_html:
Rail passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are facing disruption this week, with no train service operating on the route from Monday 10 August to Friday 14 August 2026 because of planned engineering work.

Rail replacement buses are operating between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale. Passengers can use a direct replacement service or a stopping service calling at Moston, Mills Hill and Castleton. Travellers making the full journey between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are advised to use the direct replacement bus where possible.

The disruption has prompted concern locally after passengers checking journeys discovered that their usual trains had been replaced. One post in the Rochdale Borough Noticeboard Facebook group said: ‘Just noticed there are no trains from Rochdale to Manchester this week, only replacement buses.’

The closure forms part of planned engineering work affecting services into and out of Manchester Victoria. Other Calder Valley services are operating to revised timetables, so passengers travelling beyond Rochdale should check their individual journey before setting off.

Replacement buses generally take longer than the normal rail journey and passengers should leave additional time, particularly during busy commuting periods. Anyone with onward connections is advised to check the latest timetable before travelling.

The disruption is currently scheduled to continue through Friday 14 August, with passengers advised to check National Rail or their train operator for the latest journey information before setting off.

articles.title: Vehicle Seized in Rochdale for Lack of Insurance and Licence
articles.excerpt: Officers seized a vehicle on Norreys Street in Rochdale after discovering the driver had no insurance or driver's licence.
articles.content_html:
On Monday 10 August 2026, police officers stopped a vehicle on Norreys Street in Rochdale. Officers PC Maestro, PC Bertelli, and PCSO Davies spoke to the driver during the incident.

Upon checking the driver's credentials, officers found that he had no insurance and no valid driver's licence. As a result, they seized the vehicle under relevant legislation.

The operation highlights ongoing efforts by local police to enforce road safety regulations and ensure that drivers comply with legal requirements.

Anyone with information can find Greater Manchester Police and Crimestoppers contact details at the end of this article.

articles.title: Warning Issued Over Broken Glass at Dogford Park
articles.excerpt: Dog owners are advised to exercise caution at Dogford Park due to broken glass found near the Rochdale Road entrance. The area has been partially cleared, but hazards remain.
articles.content_html:
A warning has been issued for dog owners regarding broken glass at Dogford Park. The glass is located on the grass and path area around the Rochdale Road entrance, near the traffic lights.

Local residents have reported that they have picked up as much broken glass as possible, but many shards remain scattered throughout the area. Dog owners are advised to be vigilant while walking their pets in the park.

The presence of broken glass poses a risk to both dogs and their owners, and it is recommended that visitors to the park take extra care when using this entrance.

Anyone who visits Dogford Park should remain cautious and consider using alternative routes until the area can be fully cleared of hazards.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Derker tram stop is out of service until further notice. The announcement was made on 11 August 2026 at 5:10pm.

For passengers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street to the Manchester-bound platform. Those travelling away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the lift's unavailability. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes if necessary.

Further information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Rochdale's Pioneers of Adult Education Celebrated
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's historical commitment to adult education is highlighted, showcasing the efforts of local pioneers who believed in education as a means for self-improvement and opportunity.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's rich history of adult education is being celebrated, reflecting the vision of local pioneers who viewed education as a vital resource for ordinary working people. These pioneers believed that education provided a pathway to self-improvement, opportunity, and respect.

By 1877, the Rochdale Society had established support for 14 libraries across the area, demonstrating a strong commitment to making educational resources accessible to the community. This initiative was part of a broader movement aimed at empowering individuals through learning.

The legacy of these efforts continues to influence educational practices in Rochdale today, as the community remains dedicated to fostering opportunities for lifelong learning. The impact of this historical commitment is evident in the ongoing support for adult education initiatives in the region.

As Rochdale reflects on its educational heritage, the contributions of these early advocates serve as a reminder of the importance of accessible education in shaping the lives of individuals and the community as a whole.

articles.title: Young People Engage in Community Conversation at Rochdale AFC
articles.excerpt: Young people from Rochdale Association Football Club participated in a community conversation event today, facilitated by Charlotte Delves, aimed at fostering local engagement.
articles.content_html:
A group of young people from Rochdale Association Football Club took part in a community conversation event on a bus today. The initiative was arranged by Charlotte Delves, who facilitated the visit to the Rochdale AFC Football in the Community Trust Ltd.

The event aimed to encourage local engagement and discussions among the youth, providing them with a platform to share their views and experiences.

Participants expressed their thoughts on various topics, contributing to a broader dialogue about community issues and opportunities.

This initiative reflects ongoing efforts to involve young people in community activities and discussions, fostering a sense of belonging and participation.

articles.title: Rochdale Reservoir Levels Show Signs of Recovery After Dry Summer
articles.excerpt: Reservoir levels in Rochdale are gradually rising after significant drops during an exceptionally dry summer. Recent assessments indicate that increased rainfall is helping to refill the reservoirs, although levels remain below average for this time of year.
articles.content_html:
Reservoir levels in Rochdale are showing signs of recovery after experiencing significant drops during an exceptionally dry summer. Recent assessments indicate that water levels are gradually rising, providing some relief to the local area.

The dry conditions earlier this summer led to concerns about water supply and reservoir management. Authorities monitored the situation closely, implementing measures to manage water usage effectively.

As rainfall has increased in recent weeks, the reservoirs have started to refill, although they remain below average levels for this time of year.

Local residents are encouraged to remain mindful of water usage as the recovery process continues.

articles.title: Changes to Tram Services Due to Track Repairs
articles.excerpt: Tram services will be disrupted for two weeks as track repairs are carried out between Victoria and Rochdale Town Centre.
articles.content_html:
A series of changes to tram services will take place over the next two weeks as the Bee Network undertakes track repairs. No trams will run between Victoria and Rochdale Town Centre on Saturday 15th and Sunday 16th August due to work at Monsall.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the disruption may affect travel times and connections during this period.

Further details regarding the schedule and alternative transport options will be provided by the Bee Network as the work progresses.

The repairs are necessary to maintain the safety and reliability of tram services.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches ‘Get Ready with Teddy’ Programme for Children
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has introduced the ‘Get Ready with Teddy’ programme to help children develop essential skills for starting school. Activities will take place across Best Start Family Hubs.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched the ‘Get Ready with Teddy’ programme aimed at helping children acquire key skills necessary for a smooth transition into the classroom.

The initiative will feature a series of activities designed to support children in settling confidently into school life. These activities will be available at various Best Start Family Hubs across the borough.

Parents and guardians are encouraged to participate in the programme to ensure their children are well-prepared for their educational journey.

For more information about the programme and its activities, visit the council's official Facebook page.

articles.title: Springfield Park recommended for summer visits
articles.excerpt: Springfield Park, Rochdale’s largest park, has been highlighted as an ideal summer holiday destination due to its attractions, including a miniature railway, play area, and lake.
articles.content_html:
A 42-acre park in Rochdale, Springfield Park, has been suggested as a perfect summer holiday visit. The park, located on Bolton Road, has received a Green Flag award for its cleanliness and management.

Springfield Park features a miniature railway, a play area, and a lake, making it a popular destination for families and visitors.

As Rochdale’s largest park, Springfield Park offers ample space for outdoor activities and relaxation during the summer months.

Visitors can enjoy the various amenities and natural beauty of the park, which is well-maintained and accessible to the public.
